strategy.summary: Reproduce the nnls inner-loop non-convergence in scipy/optimize/_nnls.py at buggy commit ecbd58a7ad95 by applying the PR test diff and running test_nnls_inner_loop_case1, which should raise RuntimeError (maximum iterations reached) on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed revision where the active-set check is s[P].min() <= 0. The environment uses Python 3.12 with numpy 1.26.4, the version observed in the issue traceback, and a locally built scipy; the failure is reported under MKL/AVX512 BLAS, so an OpenBLAS-only build may not reproduce it.

system_packages: libopenblas-dev or MKL (see risks: MKL/AVX512 reportedly needed)
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy.git && cd scipy && git checkout ecbd58a7ad95 && git submodule update --init
git apply test_patch.diff  (adds test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 and case2 and the _nnls.py warning-filter entry)
pip install -r requirements/build.txt && pip install -e . --no-build-isolation  (or python dev.py build)
pinned_because: numpy 1.26.4: observed in issue#20302 traceback (numpy/core/_methods.py); no documented constraint, so this pin is era-inferred from the observation and not a documented requirement
cython 3.0.8 and pythran 0.15.0: build versions named in issue#20302; documented in the issue but numerically irrelevant, so they are a convenience pin
scipy: built from the buggy commit itself, so no version pin is needed; the 1.12.0 version in the issue is era context only
pybind11: no evidence in the passages; left unpinned

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision with the test diff applied, test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 ERRORS with RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached, raised from nnls when the inner loop cycles and hits maxiter. On the fixed revision with the s[P].min() <= 0 check, the same test PASSES: nnls returns a solution and assert_allclose(dact, d, rtol=0, atol=1e-10) holds. The transition from RuntimeError to pass is the success condition.
strategy.numerical_probe: Run nnls(W @ A, W @ k) directly on the case1 inputs (n, k, A, w, W built exactly as in the test) on the buggy build and check whether it raises RuntimeError; then rerun with the 1e-10 perturbation from the comment to confirm the loop-termination sensitivity. This only confirms the mechanism; it is not graded.

input_output_examples.input: nnls(W @ A, W @ k) with n, k, A, w, W constructed exactly as in TestNNLS.test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 (N=65 lower-triangular system with zeroed rows where n_i = 0)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached.
input_output_examples.expected_output: Converged dact matching d within atol=1e-10 with no RuntimeError

risks: The reported failure depends on the BLAS/SIMD path: issue#20470 says MKL with AVX512 reproduces it, while issue#20302 used OpenBLAS (pkgconfig). An OpenBLAS build on a non-AVX512 machine may pass on the buggy revision, so the transition could not be observed there. Plan to run on an MKL/AVX512 machine, or confirm the failure first on the buggy build before trusting the transition.

The nnls inner loop is driven by floating-point rounding in the s[P].min() comparison. Without a fixed random seed or deterministic BLAS threading, the outcome may vary run to run; set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and OPENBLAS/MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 to reduce variance.

The test diff also adds test_nnls_inner_loop_case2 and test_nnls_gh20302; only case1 is in the required test_command. test_nnls_gh20302 comes from issue#20302 and may depend on later changes, so it should not be counted in the transition.
The 1e-10 perturbation workaround is reported to hide the bug but is not a fix; do not add it to the test input when checking the transition.
The passages do not state dtype, precision, or the exact stopping criterion beyond s[P].min(); the plan assumes float64 default inputs, which is not stated by the evidence.
No sanitiser or architecture requirement is documented beyond the MKL/AVX512 note; if the failure only occurs under a specific build flag, the transition will not appear on a default scipy build.

oracle.reference_source: The active-set reference in the cited Lawson-Hanson NNLS algorithm paper (constraint s[P].min() <= 0), as referenced in the PR
oracle.why: The test compares the solution against a precomputed d with an absolute tolerance, so small differences in the solution are accepted; the failure mode, however, is an exception from maxiter, not a value mismatch.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The buggy check s[P].min() <= tol keeps the inner loop cycling, so nnls exhausts maxiter and raises RuntimeError before any assertion runs; the test therefore errors on the nnls call rather than failing an assert_allclose.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the s[P].min() <= 0 check, nnls terminates, returns dact, and assert_allclose against d with atol=1e-10 holds, so the test passes.
